#!/bin/sh

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -t 1h --job-name=tools --output=tools.eo{{id}} --error=tools.eo{{id}} script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from -N 1)
# -n 1         : 1 task/CPU (from -n 1)
# -t 1h        : 1 hour time limit (from -t 01:00:00)
# --job-name=tools : job name (from -J tools)
# --output=tools.eo{{id}} : stdout file with job ID (from -o tools.eo%j)
# --error=tools.eo{{id}} : stderr file with job ID (from -e tools.eo%j)
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} or {{jobid}} for job ID instead of %j
# Note: In Flux, output and error are separate by default; combined here to match original

# Original Slurm job name: tools
# Flux: --job-name=tools

# Original Slurm output/error: tools.eo%j (combined stdout/stderr with job ID)
# Flux: --output=tools.eo{{id}} --error=tools.eo{{id}} (separate but same file)
# To truly combine stdout/stderr in Flux, both flags point to same file

# Original Slurm nodes: 1
# Flux: -N 1

# Original Slurm tasks: 1
# Flux: -n 1

# Original Slurm time limit: 01:00:00 (1 hour)
# Flux: -t 1h or -t 60m or -t 3600s

# System limits configuration
ulimit -c 0
ulimit -s unlimited

# Exit on first error
set -e

# Source environment configuration
. ~rodierq/DEV_57/MNH-PHYEX070-b95d84d7/conf/profile_mesonh-LXifort-R8I4-MNH-V5-6-2-ECRAD140-MPIAUTO-O2

# Create symbolic links
ln -sf ${SRC_MESONH}/src/LIB/Python/* .

# Module environment
module purge
module load python/3.7.6

# Execute Python script and convert images
# Note: These are sequential commands, not parallel MPI tasks
# Direct execution without flux run is appropriate for single-task jobs
python3 plot_16JAN.py
convert *.png 16JAN.pdf

# Note on execution:
# The original Slurm script runs sequential commands
# No MPI launcher (srun) was used, so direct execution is correct
# Flux will execute these commands in the allocated environment

# Complete submission command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -t 1h \
#   --job-name=tools \
#   --output=tools.eo{{id}} \
#   --error=tools.eo{{id}} \
#   script.sh

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.
The output file placeholder '{{id}}' should be verified - Flux may use '{{id}}', '{{jobid}}', or other variants depending on version. Testing recommended.

The script uses the same filename for both --output and --error (tools.eo{{id}}), which will cause both stdout and stderr to write to the same file. This matches the original Slurm behavior where -o and -e used the same pattern, but could cause interleaving issues. Consider if this is intentional.
The resource allocation is minimal (1 node, 1 task) which is appropriate for a sequential Python script and image conversion job.
No memory specification is provided. The original Slurm script also lacked memory constraints, but for image processing tasks, explicit memory allocation might be beneficial.
The script sources a user-specific configuration file (~rodierq/...) which may not be accessible if run by a different user. This is not a resource issue but a portability concern.

The symbolic link creation uses a wildcard (ln -sf ${SRC_MESONH}/src/LIB/Python/* .) which depends on the SRC_MESONH environment variable being set by the sourced profile. Ensure this variable is properly exported.
The 'convert' command (ImageMagick) processes *.png which assumes PNG files exist. No error handling if plot_16JAN.py fails to generate PNGs.
The 'set -e' will cause the script to exit on any error, which is good for catching failures but may not provide detailed error messages. Consider adding error handling or logging.
No cores-per-task specification. With -n 1, this defaults to 1 core, which matches the original Slurm specification.
The 1-hour time limit should be sufficient for the described workload (Python plotting + image conversion) but may need adjustment based on actual data size and complexity.
